basis: Governance: the centre's 13 May 2025 press release says its board appointed the managing director and calls the centre a foundation, and the Brønnøysund register lists Stiftelsen Sámi Dáiddaguovddáš as a Stiftelse.
Governance: the Brønnøysund register entry lists Stiftelsen Amandusfestivalen as a Stiftelse whose stated purpose is to hold the Amandus festival in Lillehammer.
Governance: the Brønnøysund register entry for Astrup Fearnley Museet AS lists it as an Aksjeselskap whose stated purpose is to run a museum of modern art.
Governance: the About page calls Fotogalleriet a foundation with its own board, and the Brønnøysund register lists it as a Stiftelse.
Governance: the About page says artists founded and built the house and that it is independent and artist-run, and the Brønnøysund register lists Stiftelsen Kunstnernes Hus as a Stiftelse.

Governance: the Oslo kontrollutvalget case on Kommunerevisjonen report 3/2023 (pages 1-2) says the museum is organised as a municipal agency (kommunal etat) and follows the same rules and instructions as other city agencies.

Governance: the 2024 annual report (Styrets arbeid and the section on the foundation's purpose and organisation) says it was established as a foundation in 2003, the state names the board chair and the Ministry of Culture appoints three of seven members, the foundation holds the employer role, and its purchases follow public procurement rules.
Governance: the About page calls UKS a Norwegian membership organization and a non-profit, and the Brønnøysund register lists it as a Forening/lag/innretning.
Governance: the 2025 annual report (pages 13 and 17) says Kunsthall Stavanger is a membership association (medlemsforening) and is run by Stavanger kunstforening.

Governance: the Stiftelsestilsynet supervision report of 5 March 2021 (pages 1-3 and section 4) quotes statutes sections 5 and 7 on the state-appointed board chair and three ministry members, board budget and hiring powers, and the board's hiring of the director.

Governance: the About Us page says the Zubair family established the Bait Al Zubair Foundation in 2005 to manage the museum and that it is the cultural and social arm of the family-owned business The Zubair Corporation.

Governance: the About the Museum page says Royal Decree 62/2013 established it as a legal entity with financial and administrative independence, and the Board of Trustees page lists a board formed by Council of Ministers Decision 17/2014 and chaired by the Minister of Heritage and Tourism.
